content.overview: BNS s. 328 — Punishment for intentionally running vessel aground or ashore with intent to commit theft, etc.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Punishment for intentionally running vessel aground or ashore with intent to commit theft, etc. BNS restatement of IPC 439. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 439. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 328 is the rule on “Punishment for intentionally running vessel aground or ashore with intent to commit theft, etc”. The section provides that . Whoever intentionally runs any vessel aground or ashore, intending to commit theft of any property contained therein or to dishonestly misappropriate any such property, or with intent that such theft or misappropriation of property may be committed, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 328 exists so that “Punishment for intentionally running vessel aground or ashore with intent to commit theft, etc” has a closed legal test in Chapter XVII — Of Offences Against Property. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Theft, snatching, extortion, robbery, dacoity, trust, cheating, mischief, trespass.
